title: Been experimenting with an AI trading workflow using Robinhood MCP + market-structure data from 0DTE Confluence
author: brogrammer2020
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with a platform called 0DTE Confluence recently and thought the AI/MCP side of it was pretty interesting.

What initially caught my attention was that it isn’t just another chatbot that looks at a chart and gives you a generic opinion.

The platform has a developer side with things like:

* Robinhood MCP integration
* Market and options data APIs
* MCP tools for querying market data
* Gamma rails and other market-structure data
* Confluence/confirmation information

The workflow I’ve been testing is basically giving an AI access to more structured market context instead of just asking:

“What do you think SPY is going to do?”

That seems like a much more interesting direction for AI trading.

For example, being able to ask an agent questions using actual market data and structured levels seems potentially much more useful than relying on the model’s general knowledge or uploading screenshots.

I’m curious what other people building AI trading systems think about this approach.

Would you rather have an AI trading agent:

* Query a broker through MCP?
* Query market-data APIs?
* Have access to options-chain/market-structure data?
* Combine account context with live market data?
* Use MCP tools to perform analysis without giving the AI direct trade execution?

The developer/API side is here if anyone wants to take a look:

[https://0dteconfluence.com/developers](https://0dteconfluence.com/developers)

Curious what people think of the overall architecture and whether anyone else is experimenting with similar MCP plus trading-data workflows
